intro: Four slots, all empty. Six loci above them. Is the system quiet?

steps.caption: Every slot is idle. A supervisor that reads the carriers concludes: nothing to do.
But L1 and L4 hold pending work in their mailboxes. Silence of the carriers was never evidence about the loci.
steps.takeaway: False Quiescence: declaring completion because no currently observed worker has work.

steps.caption: A sweep — not a snapshot — asks every locus whether it has admissible pending work. Two say yes. Not quiescent.
They run. The sweep repeats and finds nothing pending anywhere. Now quiescence is established, from the loci.
steps.takeaway: Quiescence is proven by a sweep over the loci; it is never read off idle carriers.

steps.caption: The tree has the pieces — CompletedSweep with a doesNotAssert field; 'a timeout abandons the request but not the work' — and not the name. PROPOSED.
steps.takeaway: A sweep carries what it does not assert; Dijkstra–Scholten is the prior art for proving termination in a distributed system.
